original_value: To get source azimuth from microphone observation angle of view in a complex real environment, this article, on the basis of the analysis of geometric positioning method, established a seven‐element microphone array model and proposed a sound source omnidirectional positioning calibration method based on microphone observation angle. By using a seven‐element array to invert the position and angle of a sound source, the relative time delay value of a pair of microphones on the vertical axis of the coordinate system is used to determine the elevation angle polarity and realize the omnidirectional sound source positioning. The array parameters, sound velocity, array size, horizontal deflection angle, elevation angle, and sound source are analyzed, and the error method is proposed. The sound source data was measured using the microphone array perspective, and a new Cartesian coordinate system was established based on the observation angle of view for omnidirectional positioning calibration of the sound source. The simulation results show that the position error of the method is about 0.01% and the angle error is about 0.005%, with high calibration accuracy. The actual measurement results show that this method can effectively calibrate the sound source azimuth, the error rate of the source coordinates is around 10%, the horizontal declination angle error is less than 5%, and the elevation angle error is less than 8%. Appropriately increasing the spacing of the array will have a better calibration effect in an actual complex experimental environment.

result.paraphrase: This paper, based on an analysis of geometric positioning methods, establishes a seven-element microphone array model and proposes an omnidirectional sound-source localization calibration method using the microphone viewing angle to obtain source azimuth in a complex real-world environment. By inverting the source position and direction with the seven-element array, the relative time delay of a microphone pair on the coordinate system’s vertical axis is used to determine the elevation-angle polarity and achieve omnidirectional sound-source positioning. Array parameters, sound speed, array size, horizontal deflection angle, elevation angle, and the sound source are analyzed, and an error method is proposed. Sound-source data are measured from the microphone-array perspective, and a new Cartesian coordinate system is established based on the viewing angle for omnidirectional localization calibration. Simulation results indicate about 0.01% position error and about 0.005% angle error, demonstrating high calibration accuracy. Actual measurements show that the method can effectively calibrate sound-source azimuth, with a source-coordinate error rate of around 10%, horizontal declination-angle error below 5%, and elevation-angle error below 8%. Increasing the array spacing appropriately yields better calibration performance in actual complex experimental environments.
